h1: SEO Agency in Birmingham: the local pack is still winnable
metaTitle: SEO Agency in Birmingham: A Local Pack You Can Win
metaDescription: Birmingham's local pack is still open in categories London closed years ago. Jewellery Quarter trades, West Midlands service areas, 90-day guarantee.
answer: Local pack competition is a function of how many verified profiles sit in your category within a searcher's radius. In inner London that count is brutal for almost every service category. In Birmingham it still isn't, for many of them — which means a well-run profile and twenty honest reviews can still put a Birmingham business in the three-pack.
takeaways: Count the competing profiles in Google Maps before you spend anything. Two minutes of counting beats a £3,000 audit.
The Jewellery Quarter is a genuine search market — hallmarking, assay and carat queries carry real buying intent.
West Midlands service-area targeting reaches Solihull, Walsall and Wolverhampton without a second address.
Multi-branch reviews don't pool. Five branches means five profiles and five review flows, run separately.

sections.h2: Which local pack categories are still open here
body: Local pack ranking is simple enough to reason about. Google returns three businesses on relevance, distance from the searcher and prominence. Distance sets the field; relevance and prominence pick the winners. So the competitive question is how many verified profiles in your category sit inside a typical searcher's radius.

In inner London that count is punishing for almost everything: accountants, cleaners, driving instructors, opticians, removals. In Birmingham the density is materially lower across most service categories, and that gap is the whole opportunity here.

Verify it yourself in two minutes rather than taking our word for it. Open Google Maps, drop the pin on your trading address, search your primary category, and count the verified listings within two kilometres. Repeat with the pin on a comparable inner-London street. The difference is what an agency is being paid to close — and if your Birmingham count is already low, much of that fee is unnecessary.

callout.title: The cheapest audit you'll ever run
callout.body: If your Birmingham category has fewer than fifteen credible competitors within a two-kilometre radius, the pack is probably winnable on primary category selection, complete profile data, service-area configuration and a steady review flow. That's a few weeks of disciplined work, not a twelve-month retainer. We'll tell you that on the first call rather than in month nine.

sections.h2: The Jewellery Quarter is a search market, not a postcode
body: The Jewellery Quarter is Europe's largest concentration of jewellery businesses and has made precious metal goods for over two centuries. The Assay Office Birmingham, founded in 1773 after Matthew Boulton's campaigning, still hallmarks there — one of four UK assay offices.

That matters because UK hallmarking is a legal requirement, not a marketing badge. Precious metal articles above the exemption weights must be hallmarked before they're described as gold, silver, platinum or palladium in trade — silver above roughly 7.78 grams, gold above one gram. Confirm the current weights with the Assay Office rather than with us.

The consequence for search is that a Jewellery Quarter retailer selling online has an unusually strong content position going spare. Buyers really do search 'what does 925 mean', 'is 9ct or 18ct better' and 'how to read a hallmark'. Those queries are high-intent for anyone about to spend four figures, and a business sitting fifty metres from the Assay Office answers them with authority no content mill can fake.

The technical half is ordinary but underdone: product schema with correct material and weight attributes, a Merchant Center feed that doesn't fight your category structure, and category pages that survive faceted navigation without spawning ten thousand near-duplicate URLs.

sections.h2: Selling to a city of family firms
body: The 2021 Census recorded Birmingham as a majority-minority city, with roughly three in ten residents identifying as Asian or Asian British. A large share of the city's SME base — retail, wholesale, food, construction, professional services, motor trade — is run by South Asian family firms across Sparkhill, Small Heath, Handsworth and Alum Rock.

We mention it because we recognise how those businesses buy — it's how most of our Indian clients buy. Referral before search. A principal who decides, not a marketing committee. Price questions early rather than late. Earned scepticism of twelve-month lock-ins. And a firm preference for talking to whoever will do the work rather than whoever won the pitch. That's less a marketing insight than a reason we fit: we already work month-to-month, we publish our prices, and the person on your call is the person on your account.

One counter-intuitive point worth the money: don't build Urdu, Punjabi or Bengali landing pages for a Birmingham audience. UK search in these communities happens overwhelmingly in English and transliterated query volume is negligible. Community language matters enormously in referral, WhatsApp and local media — which are reputation and link channels, not keyword targets. An agency pitching you multilingual landing pages here hasn't checked the data.

sections.h2: Service areas beyond the ring road
body: Most Birmingham trades sell across the West Midlands, and the profile should say so. Google Business Profile lets a service-area business list the areas it covers and hide its address entirely — the correct setup for anyone who travels to the customer. Set those areas honestly: Solihull, Sutton Coldfield, Walsall, Dudley, Sandwell, Wolverhampton, and out towards Bromsgrove or Redditch if you genuinely go there. Listing areas you don't serve produces enquiries you turn down, which is a slow way of teaching Google that your listing disappoints people.
bullets: Service-area configuration widens where you can appear; it does not override proximity. You still rank best near where you actually are.

Build a page per town only where you have something specific to say — a job you did, a rate that differs, a regulation that applies. Otherwise you're producing thin content with a place name pasted on.
If you have a shopfront customers visit, keep the address visible. Hiding it to look bigger loses you the proximity advantage you already have.

Categories drive more pack movement than most owners expect. Get the primary category exactly right before you touch anything else. [How to do local SEO](/answers/how-to-do-local-seo) covers the sequence.

sections.h2: Reviews when you have five branches
body: Multi-branch businesses are everywhere in Birmingham — garages, clinics, takeaways, letting agents, driving schools — and the review model catches most of them out. Reviews attach to a location, not a brand. Two hundred reviews on your Digbeth profile do nothing whatsoever for your Erdington one, so each branch needs its own verified profile, manager, review flow and replies. That's five times the admin, and it's the usual reason a group has one strong location and four invisible ones.
numbered: **Give each branch a named owner.** Reviews are a habit and habits need a person. Group-level ownership produces group-level neglect.
**Ask in person, at the moment of relief.** The point where the job is done and the customer is happy converts far better than an email three days later.
**Never gate or incentivise.** Filtering out unhappy customers or paying for reviews breaches Google's policies and risks the profile. It also produces a five-star average nobody believes.
**Reply to everything, especially the bad ones.** A calm reply to a one-star does more for conversion than the next three five-stars.

**Watch velocity, not just volume.** A steady trickle reads as a real business; fourteen reviews in one afternoon reads as a purchase. [Review management](/services/review-management-services) is mostly about pacing.

sections.h2: The guarantee, and the baseline behind it
body: We never promise a ranking position. Nobody controls Google's index, and in the local pack the searcher's own location is a variable no agency can touch — the same business ranks first from one street and nowhere from the next.

What we guarantee is movement against your own number. On day one we freeze your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search, taken from your CRM or call log rather than your analytics. If we haven't beaten it in 90 days, we keep working free until we do. Month-to-month after the first quarter, thirty days' notice, every asset stays yours.
That's also why we take three new clients a month and no more. A guarantee you can carry at volume isn't a guarantee — it's a marketing line with the risk quietly priced back into the fee.

faqs.q: Is the local pack easier to rank in Birmingham than London?
faqs.a: In many service categories, yes. Pack ranking depends on how many verified profiles sit in your category within a searcher's radius, and inner-London density is far higher than Birmingham's for most services. Count the competing listings in Google Maps yourself — it takes two minutes and it settles the question.

faqs.q: Do I need a Birmingham address to rank in Birmingham?
faqs.a: You need a genuine address or a genuine service area. Google Business Profile lets service-area businesses hide the address and list the towns they cover, which suits trades and mobile services. Renting a virtual office to fake proximity breaches Google's guidelines and gets profiles suspended.

faqs.q: Should I build content in Urdu or Punjabi for Birmingham customers?
faqs.a: Almost certainly not. UK search among these communities happens overwhelmingly in English and transliterated query volume is negligible. Community language matters enormously in referral, WhatsApp and local media — which are reputation and link channels, not keyword targets.

faqs.q: How do reviews work across multiple branches?
faqs.a: They don't transfer. Reviews attach to a location, so each branch needs its own verified profile, its own review flow and its own replies. That's the usual reason a multi-branch group has one strong location and several invisible ones — nobody owns the other four.

faqs.q: What does SEO cost for a small Birmingham business?
faqs.a: Our SEO starts at ₹75,000 a month ex-GST with smaller sites from ₹40,000, month-to-month after the first quarter. Convert on the day you sign. If your category count is genuinely low, we'll tell you the pack is winnable with a few weeks of profile work rather than a retainer.
